svg.aria-label: Soma roadmap from the current happy-path slice to trigger-based recovery, evidence, hardware, and product work
svg.text: Milestones — and what opens each one
Only the thin M1 happy path is current implementation scope. Every later capability needs a concrete trigger before it becomes a task.

g.text: Complete — long-term boundaries and vocabulary are documented. They guide the current slice without making every future concern implementation scope.
Research remains available as evidence; the thin Decision Register contains only choices that constrain current work.
Gate — Python commands MuJoCo through separate robot-runtime and robot-rt processes. TTL selects SafeBehavior; reset rejects the stale Plant timeline.
One model, client, command mode and local profile. No compatibility, release, recovery, or qualification promise.
Trigger — the happy path is stable and recovery is the next observed need, or representative target hardware is selected.
Then add supervision, restart/reconnect, IPC recovery, packaging, and target-derived budgets. None is an automatic sequel.
Trigger — a debugging or reproducibility workflow needs durable evidence, or the native graph is complex enough for a real Copper comparison.
Then choose the smallest useful recording and replay contract from observed needs.
Trigger — hardware becomes accessible and a real need justifies it. Classify the boundary as a NativePlantAdapter or a ManagedMotionGateway, then rerun the M1 scenarios.
A managed vendor motion boundary never inherits Soma SA-3 coverage. Inaccessible layers are published as unknown, not inferred.
Trigger — Soma owns hardware or an accessible bench. Constrained single actuator, then a synchronized multi-axis fixture, with firmware and HAL owned for every claimed layer.
Independent stop or energy-control path is chosen by hazard analysis. Early unreleased APIs may still change as physical evidence arrives.
Trigger — something exists that is worth shipping. Provisioning, signing roles, secure boot, anti-rollback, recovery; abuse and fuzz qualification; canary rollout and rollback.
The current slice remains loopback-only local development: no cryptographic mechanism is implemented or security-qualified.

svg.text: EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE FOR MILESTONE 1
Physical robot, fieldbus, E-stop, STO, hard-real-time actuation qualification · a universal URDF/MJCF/USD compiler · complete vendor emulators
Non-local security, cryptographic trust/update mechanisms · Isaac, Genesis, batch-RL infrastructure, ROS distributions · aarch64 before target selection
Fleet rollout, cloud services and UI tooling · plugin ABI and cross-version internal IPC compatibility · any safety-certification claim
These items reopen only at their named hardware, policy, security, target or product trigger.
